g.text: Landed 2026-09-24 (STATUS item 7; manager decision adopting the follow-up
review's recommended defaults): ONE pe_serdes with split payload-only
enables (TX holds on inserted stuff cells, RX skips received ones), TWO
unmodified pe_codec_mux instances clocked per ENCODED cell, half_phase as a
LEVEL with two toggles per cell, the pad overlay before the matrix's
open-drain gate, a 16-entry latched-phase window on port 0xF with separate
TXLEN/RXLEN and one-cycle tx_load/rx_start/clr strobes, and latched status
events for polling. First consumer: firmware/serdes_loop.pe +
tb_pe_soc_serdes — plain LSB/MSB, Manchester, and the directed stuffed
Manchester loopback (trailing-stuff case by construction); the new harness
regress/mutate_soc_serdes_tb.sh detects the plan's four required mutations
(TX hold, RX skip, doubled cell enable, strobe cross-wire) plus three
alignment/load defects (7/7), and regress/mutate_serdes_tb.sh guards the
split enables (7/7). Plain RX has NO phase acquisition — self-timed
wire-loopback scope only (documented limit). Reset default is
engine-disabled, so every baseline TB/firmware is bit-identical.
Closeout 2026-09-24: regress/mutate_codec_tb.sh 13/13 and the mapped STA
screen found no new violation class.
wiki/plans/serdes-integration. The eth_tx frame layer landed 2026-09-25
(Tasks 1-5) and the USB persona remains open; eth_tx plan Tasks 6-7
Landed 2026-09-24 as the R1 framed host bus (manager decision; supersedes the
A1 raw echo): SPI mode 0, MSB-first 16-bit words, 16'hA55A sync, CRC-16/
CCITT-FALSE, response opcode bit 7, sequence/target echoed. Pads: uio[4:7]
CS_N/MOSI/MISO/SCK, uo_out[1] = IRQ_N (sticky, active low), ui_in[3:5]
freed; 19 of 24 committed. The commit-latched LOAD response supersedes the
A1 uio[4] word echo. tb_pe_ctrl + pad-level tb_tt_um_protocol_emulator pass;
Landed 2026-09-25 (Manager Task 11, plan Tasks 1-5; run_all 33/33 RTL +
26/26 firmware green, synth pe_eth_tx 892 / 16,040.09 um2): pe_eth_tx emits a
full frame from firmware-supplied stored bytes (hardware 56+8 prelude, octets
LSB-first, zero pad to 64 folded into the FCS, TX-dedicated pe_crc, 8-byte
staging FIFO with underrun, runt/jabber refusal, 96-cell IFG, constant idle).
The 0xF window widened to 32 entries (push/wrap 16-23, TXLEN 24/25, TXCTRL
26, TXSTAT 27); an exclusive tx_path owner mux gates eth_start on
!ser_tx_busy and refuses tx_path clear while tx_busy; G6 reclaims uo_out[2]
(dbg_pc[0]) for the eth_tx pad behind pin_oe_bus[7]. Wire-loopback
acceptance PASS: echo len=46 field=0806 sum=07, two-frame IFG 102 idle cells
(>= 96), wrap 9 pushes REG[24]=2a REG[26]=04, busy refused_start=1.
OPEN: plan Task 6 (eth_tx mutation suites) and Task 7 (STA + close-out).
E2-6 (a macro type configured with another type's LEF passed) and R3
(corner-key vs file identity) are fixed: type <-> MACRO/cell identity checks
plus the no-shared-corner-file rule; the negative harness grew 20 -> 26
checks (type-b-wrong-lef detected as exit 1). Status: CLOSED 2026-09-24
after independent manager verification (macro harness 26/26, full
regression exit 0); R1/R4/R5 remain observations. Evidence:
29 figures across 13 act families, on a naming convention rather than a
convention-free pile: bare `proto-<act>` is the act's own figure, `-frame`
and `-timing` split it into the encoding and cell/cadence layers. Seven acts
carry all three (dht11, ds18b20, fm-biphase, freqmeter, nec-ir, servo, sr04);
the other six carry the bare figure only. The maps name the convention
instead of listing 29 nodes, because a list that long stops being a map.
MEASURED, NOT INHERITED -- and the measurement CORRECTS the brief this map
was drawn from, which listed the FREQMETER testbench as the deliberate WIP.
tb_pe_soc_freqmeter PASS: all checks -- 6 runs, 18 driven periods,
12 banked points, 158 Hz to 10 kHz, every point
tb_pe_soc_sr04 FAIL: 5 checks -- measurement 1 reads 1160 us
against a 5816 us echo, the trigger pulse is 601
clocks where 600 is required, and the firmware
banked only one of two measurements
The freqmeter is GREEN. The act that is genuinely WIP is HC-SR04, and it is
worse than red: tb_pe_soc_sr04.v is NOT wired into run_all.sh, so a green
suite is currently SILENT about it rather than reporting it.
Recorded rather than smoothed because the correction cuts against the
instruction: the project rule is that a local measurement is not a project
claim, and that cuts both ways -- a brief is not a measurement either. Both
numbers above are reproducible with one command. Flagged to the manager.
The first attempt at this measurement was a FALSE RED, and it is worth
naming: run from the repo ROOT the TB cannot open ../firmware/freqmeter.hex
and reports three failures and a watchdog. It must be run from tb/, which is
what run_all.sh does. Had that run been recorded, this note would have
A COUNT IS AN ASSERTION, and these two numbers are different kinds of thing:
* 10 PROPERTIES / 5 MODULES is what formal/results/summary.txt records,
* 11 TARGETS is that 10 plus this unlock.
Never let the target count overwrite the property count. The unlock is the
record that the pe_soc C2 owner-set guard closes under a SECOND, independent
engine (write_smt2 + yosys-smtbmc/z3), where each register has one
next-value function instead of one per sampling domain.
THE REMAINING RED, and the only one on this map. Everything else is
simulated and mapped; the physical Pico/USB board acceptance needs the
board, a shuttle and a human. The host side is explicit that 22/22 is
chip-confirmed IN SIMULATION and hardware is NOT claimed.
Landed 2026-09-25 as BLOCK 3 of the firmware-protocols work. The cell is
built from COUNTED INSTRUCTIONS, not a tick: against the 260-CLOCK UART
half-bit tick a 32 us bit is 7.38 ticks and 4.3333 us cannot express a
fraction, so midi_xfer.pe uses the timer zero times. Measured on the pin:
31,998.7 ns = 31,251 baud with a spread of 0.0000 us over all 14 frames.
Its receiver is a free-running oversampling search that VERIFIES each frame's
back-to-back 8N1 stream a falling edge is not a start bit.
Landed 2026-09-25, the mirror image: a 4 us bit is 0.923 of a tick, so
DMX is the rate the 260-CLOCK TICK cannot express. Break 88.06 us (floor
87.5), mark 12.38 us (floor 8.0), 513/513 slots with BOTH stop bits
verified, cell 3,999.8 ns = 250,010 baud, spread 0.0000 us over 513 slots.
The frame is 22.6 ms of simulated time (1.37M clocks), so the receiver
samples only inside a slot rather than free-running a strobe across it.
CORRECTION, and the correction is to the WORD 'tick', which was doing too
much work. "DMX is the rate the tick cannot express AT ALL" was true of the
260-CLOCK UART half-bit tick (port 7 STATUS, 4.33 us) and FALSE of the
other tick this SoC has: port 4 I2CTICK is a free-running 1 us counter built
from I2C_TICKS = CLK_HZ / 1_000_000 = 60 exactly (pe_soc.v:560), so it
carries 4.000 us with no rounding error at all. Read against THAT tick, the
The measured numbers are unaffected -- the act counts instructions and
programs neither tick -- but the reasoning is now stated as a fact about the
260-clock tick specifically. An earlier version of this note also said 'not
the shared tick', implying one tick; there are two, and that is the sort of
thing a reader carries into their own act.
CORRECTION, and it is worth reading because the first version of this note
was confidently WRONG. It said the R3 RTL did not exist -- "no bp_ or step
signal in pe_ctrl.v or pe_cpu.v" -- which was measured correctly and in the
WRONG TREE: this branch is behind main, and main carries the landed R3
control (21 references in pe_ctrl.v, 8 in pe_cpu.v). Generalising a local
measurement into a project claim is the exact error this block's own
findings file keeps documenting, and it is the same one the same session had
already made about the eight missing personas. Checked against main, not
against the tree that happens to be checked out.
The landed contract: DEBUG_STEP executes EXACTLY ONE instruction and is
NOT_READY (no fault) while the core free-runs; BP_SET takes one address
word, answers RANGE and changes NOTHING if the address is >= IMEM_WORDS, and
may arm while running; BP_CLR disarms, clears the hit, releases the hold,
THE BRING-UP TRAP, which is the single most useful thing on this contract
and the reason it is drawn with its own emphasis: ONCE HELD, THE run STRAP
IS IGNORED -- BOTH WAYS. A hold is released only by DEBUG_BP_CLR or by
reset. Dropping run does not resume and raising it does not either, because
(pe_cpu.v:233). A host that single-steps, stops on a breakpoint, and then
"re-asserts run=1 to carry on" finds the core STILL HELD, with no fault and
WRITE THAT GATE IN THE === FORM. The plain !dbg_hold form is the
pre-repair form and is NOT equivalent in simulation: a floating debug input
makes !dbg_hold x, the gate goes x, and the core freezes. The === 1'b1
comparisons make an UNDRIVEN DEBUG INPUT READ AS INACTIVE, and the
convention is enforced where the input is consumed rather than at every call
site -- the only place a new call site cannot forget it. Synthesis is
unaffected (x and z do not exist in hardware). Leaving those inputs
undriven took six acts to their reset after the 5b4731f merge. The
contract recorded 13 TBs then tying them low; that count is DATED -- on
today's tree 26 testbenches reference pe_cpu/pe_soc and 21 tie the debug
inputs low, the population having grown. Quote it as the contract's
Non-vacuity, which is the reason the gate exists: a proof that does not kill
its mutant is not a proof. 14 caught / 0 survived, and one eth_tx
reachability claim is labelled VACUOUS at the gate depth rather than quietly
reported as a proof. ONE OF THE FOURTEEN IS R3's: pe_ctrl_bp_hit_no_hold
CAUGHT-no-closure, so the bring-up trap has both a proof (pe_cpu_debug_hold,
inductively, claims S1-S4) and a mutant that dies without it.
CAN, JTAG, SWD, and PS/2 remain optional targets;
Built and verified standalone; integration remains
